# D10 recurrence decision sheet — Gate B0

**2026-10-17. D10 remains unapproved for implementation.** This sheet proposes product policy and a narrow next implementation scope. No native recurrence schema, command, template persistence or production behavior has been added. Observed behavior is documented in [the B0 evidence report](../tests/native-recurrence-b0-evidence.md); proposed contracts are [separate](TASK-SERVICE-D10-CONTRACTS.md).

Status vocabulary: **Established — Preserve** means a prior invariant, requiring no renewed product approval. **Recommended — Awaiting approval** means a concrete proposal, not permission to implement. **Unresolved — Additional evidence required** means the broader capability cannot enter the first engine. “Initial B” below means the proposed inactive, fresh-native implementation, not production rollout.

Evidence shorthand: **C** = current inactive core `src/commands.js`, `repository.js`, `json-repository.js`, `domain.js`; **I** = N1-B identity planning and reservations; **A** = frozen Gate A evidence/classifier; **B** = new `ItacanTaskCore/temporal/b0/evidence.json`; **N0** = owner/read/privacy contracts. B case IDs in rows refer to exact frozen observations, not native parity. Source locations/functions and limitations are expanded in the evidence report.

## Step inheritance alternatives

| Model | User-visible behavior | Benefit | Cost/risk | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: no Steps | Next task has no Steps. | Smallest implementation. | Recurring checklist disappears each time. | Reject for intended system. |
| B: copy current structure | Fresh Step IDs copy current structure/content and completion state. | Edits propagate immediately. | Accidental edits/checks/deletions become future defaults; old occurrence recompletion ambiguous. | Reject as implicit default. |
| C: copy current structure, reset completion | Fresh Step IDs copy current structure/content; every Step starts open with no binding/time. | Reusable checklist without inherited checks. | Incidental structural/content edits still propagate; which occurrence supplies the next tree after recompletion is ambiguous. | Better reset behavior, incomplete future-template policy. |
| D: explicit versioned template | New occurrence gets fresh open Steps from selected immutable revision; edits local unless explicitly promoted. | Clear defaults, stable lineage, maintainable future checklist. | Requires separate template/node identities and explicit edit action. | Recommend; not approved. |

## At-most-one successor alternatives

Generating per completion event creates duplicate tasks and Schedule entries after reopen; Oath ambiguity and event counts become coupled to retry behavior. Reusing a task UUID for all recurrences avoids a second task but loses occurrence-specific Oath/History identity. A stable predecessor generation key preserves B across new A completion attempts, lets Statistics count E2 correctly after E1 was uncounted, and makes deletion a durable deliberate action. It requires a retained ledger, explicit frontier and recovery fence, not a scan for a currently visible B.

Requiring review after every recompletion would avoid invisible duplicates but interrupt routine correction of completion state; reserve review for actual ambiguity/conflicts. An explicit second branch could preserve user intent but would need a distinct approved branching operation/key and Oath/History reconciliation; exclude branching initially. Reusing the original B unchanged provides predictable Schedule and retry behavior without introducing another task or moving a commitment. Rule edits remain explicit future-boundary operations rather than a reason to evade A's spent key.

## Approval boundary and readiness

For the initial inactive Gate B, explicitly approve D10-01/02/04/05/07/10/11/12/13/14/15/16/18/19/20 and the safe deletion/spent-key part of 17. D10-06/08/09 should at least approve the exclusions and failure distinctions so unsupported input cannot become one-off work. No approval is inferred from this document or passing specification checks. Approvals can narrow the proposed subset (for example fixed-only); the handoff must then be revised before execution.

Bounds, monthly/yearly/timed/elapsed/advanced rules, pause/resume/replace UX and legacy template adoption can remain excluded. N1-E owns historical event/current-binding import; N1-F owns native Oath adoption; N3 owns real host/activation/recovery UX; N4 owns transport and distributed conflict handling. Current recurrence quarantine stays in force for all legacy migration paths even if a fresh-native engine is later approved.

**Readiness: the evidence/specification is ready for review; a narrow fresh-native inactive implementation can be planned after explicit approvals. D10 implementation is not authorized; broader recurrence and migration are not ready. STOP FOR USER REVIEW.**
